follow-up time: Until clinical diagnosis of ASD, death, or the study end date of December 31, 2016 (mean follow-up: 9.05 years)
exposure: epidural analgesia use during labor and delivery
cohort: 388,254 singleton children born in British Columbia, Canada, between April 1, 2000, and December 31, 2014
finding: While the study found a statistically significant small increase in the risk of autism spectrum disorder in offspring of mothers who used epidural analgesia during labor and delivery, they acknowledge the possibility of residual confounding and do not consider the findings to be strong evidence for this association.
